capitals.name: Berlin
capitals.note: 'On 30 July 1945, the Allied Control Council was constituted in Berlin' (Potsdam page). The Allied-occupied Germany page names no seat for the Council, only zone headquarters (Frankfurt am Main for the American zone, Berlin-Karlshorst for the Soviet).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row for 1945 occupied Germany; Nazi Germany ends 1944). The page gives no total area, so the infobox comparison is not possible; the shape is modern Germany minus Berlin. The eastern lands are in the ledger as a loss on 2 August 1945.

correction.text: the four zones as in 1945 less the Saar, 'separated from the French zone on 16 February 1946'; Berlin's Western sectors are West Berlin

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Zone lists as of October 1946: American Bavaria, Hesse, Württemberg-Baden, Bremen; British North Rhine-Westphalia, Lower Saxony, Schleswig-Holstein, Hamburg; French Rhineland-Palatinate, South Baden, Württemberg-Hohenzollern; Soviet Saxony, Saxony-Anhalt, Thuringia, Brandenburg, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern. Bremen and Bremerhaven were exclaves inside the British zone from 1947; the Bizone (1 January 1947) merged the American and British zones in administration only.

region.text: Germany, the whole of it, before the Potsdam Agreement moved the eastern border

ledger.note: 5 June 1945: the four Allies take supreme authority over a defeated Germany. 'Germany formally surrendered on Tuesday, 8 May 1945'; the Allied administration ran 'from the Berlin Declaration on 5 June 1945'. The Potsdam page says the Allies 'assumed supreme authority by the Berlin Declaration of June 5, 1945'. The pages name no land for the Declaration, so the region (Germany with the eastern lands that Potsdam then removed) is my reading.

region.text: the three Western sectors of Berlin (479.9 km2 in the West Berlin infobox); East Berlin stays with the Soviet zone and cannot be told apart from the rest of Berlin at the grid's resolution

ledger.note: 1945: Berlin is divided into four sectors and the three Western ones, American, British and French, become West Berlin. 'The Western Allies and the Soviet Union divided Berlin into sectors in 1945'; the page gives the year only, so the month is the founding month. Berlin lay in the Soviet zone but was jointly occupied (Allied-occupied Germany page).

union.text: Württemberg-Baden, the northern halves of Württemberg and Baden (Stuttgart, Karlsruhe, Heidelberg); the page lists 'Württemberg-Baden' for the American zone

region.text: Bavaria, Hesse, Württemberg-Baden and Bremen, the American zone

ledger.note: 1945: the American zone, held by the United States. The page lists Bavaria, Hesse, Württemberg-Baden and Bremen for October 1946, headquarters at Frankfurt am Main. Year and month are the Berlin Declaration's; the zone lists are the page's for 1946, and the page says the French zone was cut from American and British land and that France traded Stuttgart to the Americans in July 1945 for Mainz and Koblenz.

region.text: North Rhine-Westphalia, Lower Saxony, Schleswig-Holstein and Hamburg, the British zone

ledger.note: 1945: the British zone, held by the United Kingdom. The page lists North Rhine-Westphalia, Lower Saxony, Schleswig-Holstein and Hamburg, 'including the Ruhr'.

region.text: Rhineland-Palatinate, South Baden and Württemberg-Hohenzollern (with the Saar until 16 February 1946), the French zone

ledger.note: 1945: the French zone, held by France. The page says France 'was at first not granted an occupation zone' and received one when 'the British and American governments later agreed to cede some western parts of their zones'; French forces had taken Karlsruhe and Stuttgart in April and May 1945, and in July France traded Stuttgart to the Americans for cities west of the Rhine such as Mainz and Koblenz. The Saar, French until 16 February 1946, is in the region.

region.text: Saxony, Saxony-Anhalt, Thuringia, Brandenburg and Mecklenburg, the Soviet zone

ledger.note: 1945: the Soviet zone, held by the Soviet Union from Berlin-Karlshorst. The Soviet occupation zone page: 'by July 1945, these gains by the British and Americans were ceded to the Soviets' under the agreed boundaries; the zone was 'established as a result of the Potsdam Agreement on 2 August 1945'.

region.text: the German territories east of the Oder-Neisse line placed under Polish civil administration (Silesia, Farther Pomerania, southern East Prussia, the Neumark); Danzig and Stettin among them

ledger.note: 2 August 1945: the Potsdam Agreement puts the German lands east of the Oder-Neisse line under Polish administration. They were 'placed under Polish and Soviet civil administration' and excluded from the Soviet zone; the cession 'included the former Free City of Danzig and the seaport of Stettin'; the final border was to 'await the peace settlement' and was fixed only by the 1990 German-Polish treaty. Signed 1 August, published 2 August.

region.text: northern East Prussia, Königsberg and the adjacent area, under Soviet civil administration

ledger.note: 2 August 1945: northern East Prussia goes under Soviet civil administration. The Potsdam page has the US and UK promising to 'support the transfer of Königsberg and the adjacent area to the Soviet Union' at the peace conference; the Allied-occupied Germany page says northern East Prussia 'later became the Kaliningrad Oblast'. The Soviet administration from 1945 is my reading of the page's 'Polish and Soviet civil administration'.

region.text: the Saar, separated from the French zone

ledger.note: 16 February 1946: the Saar is separated from the French zone. 'The Saar was part of the French zone and was separated from it on 16 February 1946'; its constitution took effect on 17 December 1947 and it joined West Germany as Saarland on 1 January 1957. The Soviet Union opposed the separation.

ledger.note: 7 October 1949: the Soviet zone is 'formally abolished with the proclamation of the German Democratic Republic'. The Allied-occupied Germany page dates the GDR to 7 October 1949 and says limited sovereignty came on 11 November 1949.

ledger.note: 7 October 1949: the German Democratic Republic is founded in the Soviet zone and the Allied-occupied Germany of the four zones is over. 'On 7 October 1949 the German Democratic Republic (GDR)' was established in the Soviet occupation zone, which was 'formally abolished' with it. The three western zones had become the Federal Republic on 23 May.

wars.name: Berlin Blockade
wars.outcome: The Soviets blockaded the Western sectors of Berlin from 24 June 1948 to 12 May 1949 and the Western Allies supplied the city by air; no border moved and no ground changed hands.
wars.note: A crisis, not a war; listed so the reviewer can see it was considered. The Allied-occupied Germany page dates the breakdown of joint control to 20 March 1948.

certainty.note: The zone lines follow Land and province boundaries fixed by Allied agreement; the Oder-Neisse border was provisional until the 1990 German-Polish treaty (Potsdam page), the lines inside Baden-Württemberg are drawn by radius around cities and are approximate.

notes: Written by eu-22-x as a state Cliopatria lacks; requested as a counterpart by eu-22-a, eu-22-e and eu-20-k. Cliopatria's Nazi Germany row ends in 1944 and the Federal Republic row starts in 1950, so 1945-49 had no German shape of record. The dossier ends in 1949 with the zones; the Western occupation of the Federal Republic to 5 May 1955 is the federal-republic-of-germany dossier's. The page gives no total area. Not settled: the dates of the individual zone boundaries and the French zone's carve-out (the page says only 'later' and 'in July'), the Western Allies' entry into Berlin, the 1947 Bremen enclave as a boundary event, the Bizone/Trizone dates (only 1 January 1947 for the Bizone), the Soviet Military Administration dates (not on the Soviet zone page). The eastern lands are modelled as lost to Poland and the Soviet Union on 2 August 1945; Poland between 1945 and 1952 has no Cliopatria row (republic-of-poland starts 1953), so the counterpart slug may need a People's Republic dossier. Gazetteer: Baden-Württemberg is split between the American and French zones with radii around Stuttgart, Karlsruhe and Heidelberg; the Lindau district of Bavaria (French zone) is not separated.
